 Lumbini set Sudurpaschim a target of 156 in NPL final
 Dilip Nath top-scored with an unbeaten 39 as the defending champions posted 155 for six, with Scott Kuggeleijn taking two wickets for the Royals.   Hemanta Shrestha/TKP bookmark facebook

 Binod Pandey 
 Published at : November 21, 2026 Updated at : November 21, 2026 18:53 Kathmandu Lumbini Lions have set Sudurpaschim Royals a target of 156 runs to win the Nepal Premier League (NPL) title after scoring 155 for six in their 20 overs in the final at the Tribhuvan University International Cricket Ground in Kirtipur on Saturday. 
 Nepal opener Aasif Sheikh once again failed to deliver for Lumbini, falling for just one run to Scott Kuggeleijn, who trapped him leg before wicket. The other opener, D’Arcy Short, scored 21 off 18 balls, hitting four boundaries. Sudurpaschim captain Dipendra Singh Airee, who came on to bowl the final over of the powerplay, dismissed Short. 
   Hemanta Shrestha/TKP Niroshan Dickwella scored 28 off 17 balls, including a boundary and two sixes, before being bowled by fellow Sri Lankan Tharindu Ratnayake. 
 Captain Rohit Kumar Paudel made 30 off 31 balls, hitting two boundaries, before being run out following a call from Dilip Nath. 
 Sundeep Jora was dismissed for four. Lumbini reached the 150-run mark after Nath and Ali Sheikh added 33 runs off 19 balls for the sixth wicket. American batter Sheikh scored 24 off 12 balls, hitting two boundaries and two sixes, before Ruben Trumpelmann came in and remained unbeaten on four off two balls. 
 Nath top-scored with an unbeaten 39 off 31 balls, including three sixes. 
   Hemanta Shrestha/TKP Kuggeleijn took two wickets to bring his tally in the tournament to 15, leaving him two behind Chitwan Rhinos’ Rijan Dhakal in the race for the leading wicket-taker award. He conceded just 25 runs in his four overs. 
 Hemant Dhami, Ratnayake and Airee took one wicket each. 
 Lumbini are seeking to defend their title, while Sudurpaschim are aiming to win the championship for the first time. Lumbini beat Sudurpaschim convincingly in last year’s final. 
 Sudurpaschim are playing their third consecutive final. They also lost the final of the inaugural edition to Janakpur Bolts. 
 Binod Pandey 
 Binod Pandey is a sports reporter for the Kantipur Publications.
